phases: Phase 1: pin the advisory contract with an executing test -- extract the boundary step's shell body by step NAME (id does not exist until Phase 2) and run it under bash -e against a recording stub at exit 0, 1, 2 and a crash with no completion line; assert the body exits 0 in every case, writes the classified boundary_rc, and invoked the scanner module with --repo.

Phase 2: make the step advisory and stop the close path overstating -- id: boundary, set +e covering every fallible command, classification on the scanner's completion line rather than the exit code, printf-based GITHUB_OUTPUT writes, REPO through env:, !cancelled() on both lifecycle steps, close condition as an enumerated allow-list of '0' and '1', and a close comment that no longer claims all checks are green.

Phase 3: record the consumer contract in the doctrine -- one paragraph under Enforcement, drafted in the plan, stating that a consumer suppresses exit 1, routes exit 2 into its own reporting path, does not use continue-on-error, and keys on the completion line because exit 1 also carries an unhandled exception.

limitations: No finding is reported to a person by this plan; a completed scan with findings writes to the run step summary and nowhere else.
Strictly better than the present state, in which nothing after the boundary step runs at all, and not the whole repair.
No test executes Actions if: semantics; the end-to-end property is pinned in two halves (body by execution, conditions by parsing).
non_goals: Anonymizing the GitHub surface (GH #431, boundary half of GH #465) -- reserved to a human operator by doctrine-publication-boundary.md:82-83.

GH #465's audit-report pairing question; GH #439 shadow-threshold remediation (operator-deferred this cycle).
